name: Five dialogue clicks in one tick
what_normally: Quests are told in pages of dialogue, and a player reads each page before clicking on, one page a tick.
what_instead: Where a page offered no choice, the run clicked blind, five times in one tick, the most the server accepts. Across every quest the plan priced that at 878 ticks.
why_allowed: The server takes five actions a tick from any player, and the swarm’s coordinator ruled the blind clicks fair.

name: Wine that ferments without a Cooking check
what_normally: Brewing wine needs Cooking level 35, and the experience arrives when a timer ferments the wine.
what_instead: The run banked stacks of unfermented wine that a helper had brewed and let the timer ferment them all at once. In the last attempt the first firing took Cooking to 60, and the second, one relog later and about 15 seconds after it, to 99.
why_allowed: The fermenting timer is a game script with no level check, so it pays out at any level.

name: Working through the Thieving stun
what_normally: Pickpocketing a knight sometimes fails, and a failure stuns the thief for 11 ticks in which they cannot steal.
what_instead: In the run each stocked stun cast Superheat Item on ore twice, then Charge, then fletched arrows, while a courier beside the knights brought the ore, food and arrowheads; Magic and Fletching both reached 99 inside the Thieving step. The lab measured the first form, three bone burials with Charge and arrows in every stun: Thieving took no longer, and 470 to 510 ticks of other work moved inside it.
why_allowed: The stun blocks stealing, not burying, casting or fletching.

name: Charge, recast with no cooldown
what_normally: Charge is a Magic spell unlocked by the Mage Arena quest, and a spell normally makes its caster wait before the next cast.
what_instead: Charge has no wait, so it can be cast again at once: in the lab, Magic went from 80 to 99 in 156 to 163 casts over 32 to 33 ticks. In the run, Charge went inside the Thieving stun pack, one or two casts a stun, and Magic reached 99 about 85 seconds into the Thieving step.
why_allowed: Each cast is a legal click, and the spell’s script checks no timer.

what_normally: Protect from Melee is a prayer that blocks close-combat hits, and it drains prayer points for every tick it stays on.

name: Logged-out time is free
what_normally: Most races are timed by a clock on the wall.
what_instead: This hiscore times an account by the in-game tick of its last level-up, and only logged-in ticks count. The run logged out between steps, so waits of up to nine hours for helpers and fixes cost nothing.
why_allowed: It is the hiscore’s own rule.
sources: data/attempts-timeline.json, attempt 5 (holds of 9 h 08 min, 5 h 50 min and 6 h 46 min)

name: Quests picked for what they unlock
what_normally: Quests are optional stories, taken in any order.
what_instead: The route took Mage Arena for the Charge spell and Dwarf Cannon for the cannon, ordered the rest by what they unlock and how far apart they are, and moved Agility from 75 to 99 to the very end.
why_allowed: Quest order is the player’s choice.

name: One tick per dialogue page, not two
what_normally: The standard bot client spent two ticks on every dialogue page, one to see it and one to click.
what_instead: The swarm’s client publishes the game’s state once a tick, so the click goes out in the tick the page appears.
why_allowed: The fix is in the bot’s own client, and the server sees the same click a tick sooner.

name: The knife-on-logs reset
what_normally: With a rune axe on a willow, the game rolls for a log every 4 ticks.
what_instead: One tick after each roll the bot uses a knife on its logs, picks a fletching option, drops a log and clicks the tree again, all in one tick. The next roll comes 3 ticks after the last, and the menu closes before anything is spent.
why_allowed: Opening the fletching menu rewrites the player’s action timer, and the woodcutting script trusts that timer.
sources: rs-sdk docs/speedrun/research/tick-manipulation.md lines 39-59 and 160-194 (willow 5.53 to 4.23, 131 gaps; fly fishing 5.56 to 3.80; iron 4.94 to 3.00 at the demo’s respawn)

name: The knife reset on a slow server
what_normally: The reset works only when the server answers on time, and the live server was sometimes slow.
what_instead: Each woodcutting and mining band ran a small program inside the game page that counted how many of 20 actions landed on time. Below 14.5 it fell back to plain cutting, unless the band was burying bones, which only the knife loop can do.
why_allowed: The program sends the same clicks a player could.

name: Fitting extra actions into the gathering rhythm
what_normally: A gathering skill keeps its rhythm only while the player clicks the tree or rock again on the right tick, and using an item normally breaks it.
what_instead: The run sent its extra actions earlier in the same tick as the gathering click, so the click landed last and the rhythm held.
why_allowed: The server handles a player’s actions in the order they arrive, up to five a tick.

name: A run host 3 ms from the server
what_normally: The game server sits in a data centre in Virginia, and from Southern California a click takes 80 to 90 ms there and back, so a reaction often misses the tick it was meant for.
what_instead: The run’s bot ran on a machine in the same data-centre region, about 3 ms away, so a reaction to one tick landed in the next.
why_allowed: Anyone can rent a machine near the game’s server.
failed_live: In the rehearsal the run host’s nine-hour session limit ran out, and the account dropped 13 times.
